svg.title: The Land Flip Acquisition Loop
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-land-flip-core-process; chapter number: 1; chart type: process_flow; title: The Land Flip Acquisition Loop; subtitle: From liquid county to verified contract in five operator steps; caption: Land flippers pick counties with real sales velocity, scrub out unbuildable parcels, price off per-acre comps, lead with texting, and verify access, septic, and funding before money goes hard.; assumptions note: Step order consolidates the workflows described by the cited practitioners; every threshold shown is an attributed practitioner claim, not a universal market rule.; note: Attributed to Thomas | Land Flipping (ZfyoS572Kbk), Landon Bleau via REtipster (Uaqe67xWZN0), Seth Williams of REtipster, Clayton Hepler via DealMachine Podcast (HE45qWS8txg), and Ron Apke via Real Estate Pros Show (Z_ZynszdCFo).; stages: step: 01; label: Pick Liquid Counties; value: Step 1; detail: Thomas pulls lists only in counties with at least 200 land sales a year and fewer active listings than sold listings; lists under 1,000 texts get bundled with neighboring counties.; step: 02; label: Scrub Unbuildable Parcels; value: Step 2; detail: Strip the 40% to 50% of parcels carrying wetlands, flood, slope, or bad access before any offer is built.; step: 03; label: Price Off Median Per-Acre Comps; value: Step 3; detail: Build offers from median price per acre minus agent, closing, and lender costs; Seth Williams teaches buying at 5% to 30% of value while Clayton Hepler offers 50% to 55%.; step: 04; label: Text First, Mail Second; value: Step 4; detail: Landon Bleau reports about 9x return on ad spend for texting versus about 3x for mail; cutting texts to about 100 characters lifted reply rates from 13%-15% to nearly 20%.; step: 05; label: Verify Access, Septic, and Funding; value: Step 5; detail: Confirm legal deeded access, verify soil and septic (Thomas paid about $600 per test and now has the buyer verify in inspection), line up funding, and amend closing by 30 to 45 days rather than let earnest money go hard on an unsold deal.
